title: customer escalation war room - Delta Insurance - 2026-04-06 notes
content:
War room notes - Delta Insurance (customer)

Date: 2026-04-06
Reported by: Delta SRE (internal)
Severity: P1 - large % of requests failing with 502s -> impacting claims-processing queue
Initial incident start: ~2026-04-06 02:40 UTC
First customer report received: 2026-04-06 03:10 UTC
War-room convened: 2026-04-06 03:25 UTC (this doc)

Attendees (quick list): Priya Natarajan (CS, owner), Liam O'Connor (Solutions Eng), Jules Park (Product - Hosted API), Marco Ruiz (Serving-runtime eng), Sara Li (SRE on-call), Delta SRE: Abhilash Rao (on-call)

Quick objective: stabilize customer traffic to <1% error, create short-term mitigation, identify root cause, define fix and rollout plan.

What we know so far (observations):
- Errors are 502 from Redwood gateway to serving-runtime for model `redwood-tt-large-v1` only.
- Error spike correlates with a config rollout (auto-scaling policy change) at ~02:35 UTC (recent change: increase min-pools for Dedicated).
- Delta traffic pattern: bursty batch of long-context document embeddings + generation requests during nightly ingestion window.
- Logs show KV cache thrashing: repeated cache misses + eviction warnings in runtime logs.
- Memory pressure increased on a subset of nodes -> OOM-kill on one GPU host at 02:39 UTC, restarted, causing transient 502s.

Hypothesis (working):
- Recent autoscaling/pool config change increased packing of long-sequence requests onto fewer nodes, causing KV cache size/eviction thrash and memory pressure -> OOM and 502s. Serving runtime didn't gracefully shed load in that scenario.

Immediate mitigations attempted / results:
- Rollback config: Jules rolled back the autoscaling change at 03:05 UTC -> reduced new node packing but errors persisted for ~15m due to unhealthy nodes.
- SRE (Sara) cordoned and drained affected host at 03:15 UTC -> reduced 502s, error rate dropped from 18% -> 4%.
- Traffic routing: Liam enabled fallback route to `redwood-tt-medium-v1` for non-critical ingestions at 03:20 UTC -> immediate relief for backlog (approx 30% of requests routed).

Decisions (agreed):
- Keep rollback of autoscaling change until root cause confirmed (action: Jules, due 2026-04-06 12:00 UTC).
- Maintain fallback routing for ingestion window until SAFE(3) tests pass (action: Liam, due 2026-04-07 03:00 UTC).
- Pause any further model-variant rollouts for Delta until postmortem (action: Priya -> notify customer; due 2026-04-06 09:00 UTC).

Action items (owner — clear due dates):
- Marco Ruiz: investigate KV cache eviction metric behaviour and memory pressure link to packing heuristics. Look at timeline 01:00-04:30 UTC. Deliver initial findings and logs snippet to this doc. Due: 2026-04-06 10:00 UTC.
- Sara Li: follow up on the drained host, check for residual degraded hosts, confirm cluster healthy state and whether automatic restarts will return. Provide snapshot of node states and OOM details. Due: 2026-04-06 08:00 UTC.
- Jules Park: keep autoscaling config rollback in place and prepare a safe rollout plan with staged canaries + metrics gating (KV eviction < X, mem pressure < Y). Draft plan due: 2026-04-07 12:00 UTC.
- Liam O'Connor: maintain fallback routing, collect customer-visible error-rate/time-to-resolution metrics, and coordinate with Delta SRE to throttle non-critical ingestion if needed. Update due: 2026-04-06 15:00 UTC.
- Priya Natarajan: prep customer update (timeline + mitigation steps + ETA for fix), send to Delta CSM and engineering contact. Due: 2026-04-06 09:00 UTC.
- Delta SRE (Abhilash Rao): provide ingestion batch schedule and expected burst sizes, share sample request traces for 02:00-04:00 UTC. Due: 2026-04-06 11:00 UTC.

Notes / open questions to resolve:
- Does the serving runtime respect per-model KV cache limits correctly under autoscaling packing? (Marco)
- Is there an interaction between the new packing heuristic and quantized model memory footprint estimates? (Marco + runtime perf)
- Can we add temporary request-level circuit breaker to refuse extremely long-context ingestion batches during nightly window? (Product + Runtime)
- Need to confirm whether customer's on-prem VPC Private deployment has any networking differences contributing to timeouts (Delta team to confirm).

Communication plan:
- Short customer update (Priya) once we confirm cluster healthy + rollback in place (ETA 09:00 UTC).
- Follow-up technical postmortem and timeline to be published to Confluence after full RCA (owner: Marco + Jules). Target publication: 2026-04-09.

Next check-in (internal): 2026-04-06 11:00 UTC (30 min sync) — quick status and go/no-go on routing rollback.

Post-meeting quick log capture (for traceability):
- Snapshot of gateway error rates (Chart ID: gw-err-delta-0426) attached in Confluence.
- Runtime logs collected: runtime-logs-delta-2026-04-06-02-00-04-30 (S3 internal path referenced in Confluence page).

Misc notes (scratch):
- Customer is in production for claims; SLA discussions may be needed if prolonged.
- Consider temporary increased burst capacity for Dedicated pool for Delta during ingestion window if this is a recurring pattern (commercial/infra discussion).

If you are assigned an action, paste updates below (timestamped). Use this doc as single source for war-room updates.

---
Update log:
2026-04-06 06:05 UTC — Marco: initial KV eviction graph attached to Confluence. Seeing correlated spikes with long requests. (will analyze more)
2026-04-06 07:20 UTC — Sara: drained host remains offline, but cluster healthy after rebalancing; no new OOMs since 03:40 UTC.
2026-04-06 08:45 UTC — Priya: customer update sent to Delta CSM (cc: customer-eng). They acknowledged and will throttle some non-critical jobs during night window tomorrow.
